Coulda, shoulda, woulda. I'm afraid that companies that think like this are probably not going to be too abundant for some time yet - especially not one like Nintendo. Nintendo's as old as the hills, and likes its control something fierce (see: Game Genie lawsuits, which are before the time of a lot of Voaters, but were pretty nasty), and this is going to require both a change in shareholder mindset and all of the old guard to be replaced (probably retire), and this is going to have to happen industry-wide before any of this happens.

There are a few companies that have engaged in this and have come up with great results - Final Doom was entirely fan-made, with id hiring the two best WAD making teams around and having them build an entire game based on the Doom 2 engine. And the rabid loyalty and creativity of fans is documented in a most spectacular fashion across many genres and fictional sources. However, most executives can't seem to grasp the thought of the fan mindset outside of how to have marketing convince them to pull in enough revenue to bump up profits for the next quarter regardless of long-term consequences.

Myself, eons ago, I'd have paid a substantial amount of money to buy Nintendo 64 games for the PC. Unfortunately, they didn't want my money, apparently.

I strongly recommend watching Halt and Catch Fire to anyone who wants a glimpse in to the corporate mindset. It's a story set in the 80's during the initial PC boom before open architecture had become a thing, and it's absolutely brilliant.

The short of it is that old corporations often miss the boat entirely on paradigm shifts in the technology sector.
